ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, inputs A and B respectively branch into the upper “&” gate; the output of this upper “&” gate continues into a box marked “1”, and the output end of this box has a small inversion circle. A and B also simultaneously enter the lower gate marked “≥1”; the output of the lower gate is connected to one input end of the final “&” gate on the right. The upper branch with inverted output is also connected to the other input end of the final “&” gate. The output end of the final “&” gate likewise has a small inversion circle, and the output is labeled Y. Reasoning: The output of the upper “&” gate is X1 = AB; its subsequent output end has an inversion bubble, so the upper signal sent into the final gate is X2 = overline(AB). The lower “≥1” gate means at least one input is 1, that is, an OR gate, so the output is X3 = A + B. The final “&” gate first ANDs X2 and X3, obtaining (A + B)·overline(AB), and then the inversion bubble at the final output end inverts this product. Therefore Y = overline((A + B)·overline(AB)).

method.method_draft: First assign intermediate signals from the image: the upper '&' gate gives X1 = AB, and because its following block has an output inversion bubble, the signal into the final gate from the top is X2 = overline(AB). The lower '≥1' gate receives A and B, so its output is X3 = A + B. The final '&' gate combines X2 and X3, and its output bubble complements the product. Therefore write Y = overline((A + B) · overline(AB)).
